{{family name hatnote|Guo ''(过)''|lang=Chinese}}
'''Zeng-Yuan Guo''' ({{zh|c=过增元|p=Guò Zēng-yuán}}), born 20 February 1936 in [[Jiangsu Province]], is a professor in the Department of Engineering Mechanics (School of Aerospace) in [[Tsinghua University]], [[Beijing]], China. He is a member of the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]] (1997) and a [[ASME Fellow|ASME fellow]] (1998).<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.tsinghua.edu.cn/chn/szdw/gzy.htm |title=清华大学 |access-date=2016-03-17 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304063727/http://www.tsinghua.edu.cn/chn/szdw/gzy.htm |archive-date=4 March 2016}}</ref>

== Academic contributions ==
Guo's work has been focused in [[Thermofluids|thermofluid]] mechanics, [[heat transfer]] processes at the micro and nano scales, optimization of [[thermodynamic system]]s, and more efficient thermal transport.<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |last=Zhang |first=Xing |year=2011 |title=In Celebration: Professor Zeng-Yuan Guo, Chinese Academician, on his 75th birthday |url=http://hamadayama.tokyo/Guo_75.pdf |journal=[[International Journal of Heat and Mass Transfer]] |volume=54 |pages=753–754 |doi=10.1016/j.ijheatmasstransfer.2010.09.062 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200912174832/http://hamadayama.tokyo/Guo_75.pdf |archive-date=2020-09-12 |via=[[Elsevier]]}}</ref> In 1994 he introduced the concepts of thermal drag, thermal drive, thermal displacement, and [[thermal instability]], which use analogies to mechanical systems to describe properties in thermal systems.<ref>{{Cite book|url=http://www.dl.begellhouse.com/references/5756967540dd1b03,6bc03fbe0b7a0bf3,15f480e37f2f3704.html|title=Annual review of heat transfer|publisher=Begell House|year=1994|isbn=978-0-8493-9905-3|editor-last=Chen|editor-first=Gang|pages=207–270|chapter=Thermally Induced Effects on Fluid Flow|volume=5 |issue=5 |doi=10.1615/AnnualRevHeatTransfer.v5.70 |issn=1049-0787|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200912175532/http://www.dl.begellhouse.com/references/5756967540dd1b03,6bc03fbe0b7a0bf3,15f480e37f2f3704.html|archive-date=2020-09-12}}</ref>

=== Thermomass theory ===
{{See also|Thermal conduction}}
Thermomass theory models [[heat transfer]] as a gas-like flow from heat carriers, caused by a [[pressure gradient]]. In this framework, heat has a dual nature, acting as mass during transfer and as energy during transformation.<ref name=":0" /> This approach has been applied, for example, in modeling heat conduction in [[Nanosystems Engineering|nanosystems]], where non-local, non-linear effects not fully accounted by [[Fourier's law]] [[heat equation]] and by the [[Relativistic heat conduction#Hyperbolic model|Maxwell-Cattaneo-Vernotte equation]] are more significant.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Sellitto |first1=A. |last2=Cimmelli |first2=V.A. |editor1-last=Tzou |editor1-first=Robert D. |title=A continuum approach to thermomass theory |journal=Journal of Heat Transfer |date=November 2012 |volume=134 |issue=11 |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/274875043 |publisher=The American Society of Mechanical Engineers|doi=10.1115/1.4006956 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Freitas |first1=R. S. M. |last2=Stampa |first2=C. S. |last3=Lobão |first3=D. C |last4=Alvarez |first4=G. B. |title=Numerical Study Concerning Thermal Responses of Nanofilms under the Thermomass Theory |journal=Thermal Engineering |year=2016 |volume=15 |issue=1 |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/316527836 |publisher=Brazilian Society of Mechanical Engineering and Sciences}}</ref>

In 2013, Prof. Guo's group was granted major project funding by the [[National Natural Science Foundation of China]] for their work in developing thermomass theory.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Guan |first1=Nanxiang |last2=Wang |first2=Bing |last3=Li |first3=Luming |title=A brief overview of the School of AerospaceEngineering of Tsinghua University |journal=Chinese Journal of Aeronautics |date=September 2018 |volume=31 |issue=9 |pages=1805–1814 |doi=10.1016/j.cja.2018.07.005 |s2cid=125466567 |doi-access=free |bibcode=2018ChJAn..31.1805G }}</ref>

=== Entransy ===
The concept of entransy, developed by Guo's group, is based on an analogy between [[electrical conduction]] and heat conduction. Their work in "Entransy dissipation in [[heat exchanger]]s" was included in the top 10 research fronts in mathematics, computer science and engineering by [[Thomson Reuters|Thomson-Reuters]] in 2014.<ref>{{Cite web|date=December 2014|title=Research Fronts in 2014: 100 top ranked specialties in the sciences and social sciences|url=http://ir.las.ac.cn/bitstream/12502/7451/1/Research%20Fronts%20English_FINAL.pdf|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200912181542/http://ir.las.ac.cn/bitstream/12502/7451/1/Research%20Fronts%20English_FINAL.pdf|archive-date=2020-09-12|access-date=2020-09-12}}</ref>

The concept of entransy has been accused of plagiarism as well as criticized for being incorrect and a hoax, by [[Adrian Bejan]] and others, with Milivoje Kostic writing a critical perspective on the issue.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Kostic|first=Milivoje M.|date=July 2017|title=Entransy concept and controversies: A critical perspective within elusive thermal landscape|url=https://www.kostic.niu.edu/kostic/_pdfs/Entransy-Concept-Contraversies-IJHMT.pdf|journal=International Journal of Heat and Mass Transfer|volume=115|pages=340–346|doi=10.1016/j.ijheatmasstransfer.2017.07.059 |bibcode=2017IJHMT.115..340K |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200913140306/https://www.kostic.niu.edu/kostic/_pdfs/Entransy-Concept-Contraversies-IJHMT.pdf|archive-date=2020-09-13|via=Elsevier}}</ref>

== Awards ==
Early in his career, Guo received a [[Humboldt Research Award]] from the [[Alexander von Humboldt Foundation|Alexander Von Humboldt Foundation]] to work in the [[Technical University of Munich]] between 1979 and 1981.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Prof. Dr. Zeng-Yuan Guo|url=https://www.humboldt-foundation.de/en/connect/explore-the-humboldt-network/singleview?tx_rsmavhsolr_solrview%5BpPersonId%5D=1015469&cHash=e8b5defafa718805140a254c439ae3e4|url-status=live|archive-url=https://archive.today/20200911130641/https://www.humboldt-foundation.de/en/connect/explore-the-humboldt-network/singleview?tx_rsmavhsolr_solrview%5BpPersonId%5D=1015469&cHash=e8b5defafa718805140a254c439ae3e4|archive-date=11 September 2020|access-date=2020-09-11|website=Alexander von Humboldt-Stiftung Foundation}}</ref> One of the first Chinese members of the [[American Society of Mechanical Engineers]], he was named a Fellow in 1998.<ref>{{Cite web |title=The ASME Fellow |url=https://www.thefreelibrary.com/THE+ASME+FELLOW.-a057951045 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200912140842/https://www.thefreelibrary.com/THE+ASME+FELLOW.-a057951045 |archive-date=2020-09-12 |access-date=2020-09-12 |website=[[The Free Library]]}}</ref> In 2017 he received an Outstanding Achievement Award from the Asian Union of Thermal Science and Engineering for his life-time dedication to the area.<ref>{{Cite web|title=AUTSE Awardee|url=http://autse-asia.org/?page_id=493|url-status=live|archive-url=https://archive.today/20200912141038/http://autse-asia.org/?page_id=493|archive-date=12 September 2020|access-date=2020-09-12|website=Asian Union of Thermal Science and Engineering}}</ref>
